Under the heading of Memorie, though the content was different, the Foundress kept with care even the personal notes she made on the visits to the houses. In a textbook entitled Fragments of Memorie, dated from 1881 to 1884, a long series of observations were made from what seems an occasion of a meeting of the superiors. A precise indication of the date: “November 18, 1884” follows and subsequently another dated: 27th and 28th of September; it will not be difficult to verify the year because she speaks of visits to some houses of Sicily.

Another booklet starts with January 1, 1887 and contains the notes regarding the visits to Naples in the Abruzzi and in Sicily, then those she made in Florence (28 July) Prato, Pistoia… In the second part of booklet 7, a bit miscellaneous, we find a trace of 28th of September, from some arguments to be treated in the near Chapter (the one of 1888). In the month of May 1888 she restarts the observations on the visits: Sassuolo, Parolise, Pisa, and Genoa… After she goes back to the month of May; she narrates briefly her journey to France and finishes reporting a letter to a reverend father, not identified well, on certain relevant points regarding discipline and another one to a superior, certainly of another Congregation, in which she tells exactly the timetable of the respective community.

Booklet 8 of the Memorie comments on some of the visits of 1889 and 1890. Finally there is a booklet, started on September 18, 1888, a real note-book of brief notes and memorandum regarding the transfer of the sisters and other particulars related to the practical organization of the work.

The sense of concreteness that shines in the letters of Mother Rosa Gattorno results in a remarkable way from these notes, written with liveliness and even with rawness. Certainly the image of the communities – and concretely of the superiors – the way it comes out of these pages appears to us hardly flattering. Since Mother Rosa gave much importance to the conscience of those responsible, the superiors and to the good example that they should give, she obviously suffered when she discovered one of them incoherent. But it was not easy to find religious that could measure up to such assignment given the rapid growth of the Institute not only in Italy but also in America and in Africa. The harshness of the expressions is tuned to the style of her temperament, vehement, sincere, and straightforward. It should be kept in mind that these reproaches were reserved to the superiors exclusively; therefore they did not include the other sisters.

As Foundress, aware of her mission Rosa Gattorno actively assisted by Father Tornatore, was concerned right from the beginning about the human and spiritual formation of the sisters that the Lord gave her. From the first years, in fact, Mother Rosa in her Memoirs mentions about her conferences to the sisters; she certainly did not possess the theological bases of the Co-founder but she had the gift on the charismatic level of being really able to transmit to her daughters what she lived and contemplated and what she wanted to obtain from each one of them. She experienced this magisterium as something which was above her capacities; she considered herself the pure instrument of God who enlightened her mind and put in her mouth the right words. She explains it amply in the month of April 1874:

“I cannot omit to record what the Lord does in me when I have to give a conference to the Daughters of St. Anne. It is enough for me to gather my thoughts and to stand before my Crucifix: your ignorant slave must speak and talk on the subject of perfection; you my beloved Master, must tell me what to say and I will repeat it. And something happens in me that if those listening to me were to see it they would be amazed… he comes close to me; often he dictates to me things from the Holy Scripture which I did not know… I often appreciate the things I say myself. At other times I do not; I speak in the third person and I do not understand what I am saying…”

From the end of 1888, after the dismissal of Father Tornatore, the Foundress assumed fully the responsibility of the formation through the circular letters as well as the weekly conferences and the special instructions to the superiors on the occasions of her regional visits. The themes were about all the aspects of formation: personal and social behavior, sacramental catechesis and ascetism and meditation; but the preferred theme of the sisters was that of God’s love. Among the booklets of the Memoirs, just because it is a question of personal remembrances, the Servant of God wanted to keep the schemes of many conferences given to the sisters from 1888 to1898. Most of these outlines are summaries made after the conference, that is, according to the light received from God. They are the writings which better help us to measure the spiritual dimension of Rosa Gattorno, her real spiritual magisterium. But to understand well all these dimensions one needs to bring alongside the original schemes the notes of the conferences and meditations taken by the secretaries that are kept in the Archives of the Institute like all the other writings.

Date 16 December, Sunday. 2nd chapter of the Rule. At the end of the reading, only a few lines, I started. I know that before I was able to say anything, but my Good knew how to put into my mouth, words that are fit, that I found myself repeating a discourse about his coming and his love; who could repeat it? Not I because I heard that a smooth speech was coming out of my mouth, but since it was not mine, I was not able to keep anything in my mind. I can say that while I went to make such a conference I had nothing in my mind. // I could even say that it was empty and I was asking myself what I would have said because I was not able to gather anything.

My Love, I will fear no more, but with the usual confidence with which I carry out the other things, without any knowledge, I will do the same with this, knowing that you speak through this poor creature who lives and works only for you. I am nothing and less than nothing, but with you I know

I can do everything, my Love, Being of my life, my Jesus! //

25 December 1888: Christmas. 3rd Conference

3rd chapter of the Rule. I spoke of what a child felt in receiving Jesus and of how much a holy religious questioned by the superior saw on Christmas night in the religious. She was questioned, if Jesus came into the heart of all and she answered no. He only came into the heart of the child, of the superior and of this saint, and not into the others. This was the theme; I do not know how I carried it,

I can only say that I really wanted to speak of the love of Jesus, but I tried to control myself and my Good was speaking. I felt much strength in me… In fact I suffer no want and I do not faint. //

January 1889, Sunday. 4th Conference

4th chapter of the Rule. Objective: to achieve G. Sp

(Jesus Spouse).

Tell me, did you become a religious to be holy? Well, take your cross, bow your head and go forward to work!

The earth is vast, and the field immense; enter and go ahead and never look back, look at what is to be done. It is a bad thing to believe you have done something! How could nothing do something?

The Novices should all be full of fervor and well nourished in the spirit of the Work of the Lord etc… //

Sunday 6 January 1889. 5th chapter of the Rule. 5th

Conference on the three vows of chastity, poverty and obedience. Chastity is the gold that the Virgin offers to

God; poverty is the myrrh because observing and putting into practice this vow, we offer the perfume of our abstinences to God; in this way we trample down the comforts and what could softly satisfy us. Obedience is the incense that spreads the perfume of all the virtues put together; obedience! Perfect denial of our will. //

Monday 14 January 1889. 6th Conference: on the manner of confession and what disposition one needs to have in such a court; how one should accuse herself, what one should say when questioned in affairs which do not regard us. I stressed on that point of Rule which says never to speak about the confessor with the sisters.

The superiors must be very careful, because disorder always comes from this etc. //

20 January 1889. 7th Conference: on the vow of poverty. How should it be interpreted? I tried to explain it to my level best and after I said how difficult it was to put it into practice and how much creatures are easily attached to many things. Human nature is such that it is attracted by the smallest thing. //

27 January 1889. 8th Conference: on the vow of chastity.

For this precious treasure much purity is obtained from the meditation and therefore it must be taught what effects the ordinarily well done meditation upon death, judgment, heaven and hell can have. After I will ask how one did it, what does she consider, what effects did this produce if she meditated and felt the effects of the meditation in her heart and in her mind. In the same way I will call on more than one to say something on the effects of Communion. For the Novices, when they do not do it, what their hearts feel and if they unite themselves to those who do it // or if they remain indolent. As the thirsty deer longs for a spring to quench itself, the same is in deprivation…

Other words to explain this point? My Good will have to take care, because I am not capable; I walk gropingly, my light brightens the way and I walk frankly. //

2 February 1889. 9th Conference: on the vow of obedience. Here my God, the Good of my soul made me say things that I did not even dream of knowing. Oh, what bounty to lower himself to make me speak meaningfully, a miserable creature as I am capable of nothing!

Many questions were made on meditation and other teachings were given to the novices as how they should meditate and also for the Communion. They were exhorted to think about the vow of obedience on all the eight days and to make commitments and questions. //

3 February 1889. 10th Conference: the vow of poverty.

How it was appreciated by the saints and by the souls who sought perfection and how it should be practiced.

On the chapter of silence: how Jesus speaks to our heart in the silence. I carried out this theme and concluded it by calling the sisters for meditation explaining it to them… //

10 February 1889. 11th Conference: mortification of gluttony. Remarks on how easy it is to commit sins of gluttony and how Jesus is pleased with these mortifications, even if small, which do not cost us much but which have much value.

I would like to write whatever I said, but it is not possible for me since it is not my stuff and it is difficult for me to keep in mind whatever I say.

The usual questioning was done on meditation and then other small things were said. //

17 February 1889. 12th Conference: chapter of the Rule on cloister.

It was explained what our cloister should be. Examples were brought and then it was said how the Holy Mother commands one not to go to the room of the other one and what happens if this takes place. Then it was passed to the questions on the meditation, and they were taught how to do it and how to do it well with profit.

24 February 1889. 13th Conference: The confessions and the confessors. I tried to show the damage done to the soul by speaking of the confessor among us. This is not only failure against the Rule, and this should be enough, but it still brings many evils and remarkable faults are made. They were taught to confess and how they should confess in order to make a good confession for profit and grace. In addition one should not seek to have one priest rather than another. They are all ministers of the Lord and we should not have preferences. //

3 March 1889. 14th Conference: chapters 2 and 3 of the Rule. I tried to show them the value that prayer done in common has; how it pleases God and has advantages. I also said that they should be prompt and never miss them. I spoke of the custom we have, that of asking the superior for receiving Communion. We must certainly do it always if we have the permission of the confessor; this act of humility pleases the Lord much. //

10 March 1889. 15th Conference: chapters 4 and 5 of the Rule. I explained what kind of affection the Daughter of St. Anne should have and what reward they will receive from the Holy Mother. In addition how we should be grateful to Jesus and Blessed Mary; how the graces which we ask through the saint, and the prayers for the dead especially for our sisters should be done was explained.

Then, meditation was considered especially on death which should not frighten us but be of comfort and help us to amend our imperfections. //

31 March 1889. 16th Conference: article 4 on the practice of the virtues; the first of the theological virtues. What I was told on this point I am completely unable of writing down because I remember nothing. As I finished this conference I even felt disheartened because I was sure of having said nothing good and of having neither sufficient effect nor having convinced the hearts of the sisters leaving in them a gap and having annoyed them. Oh, what pain I felt!

When I heard that it was not annoying at all I said: may my Love be eternally blessed! //

7 April 1889. 17th Conference: simplicity and prudence.

My Good said many things on simplicity; he showed me how the simple minds and hearts pleased him and how this simplicity should be. Then he passed to prudence of the simple person and showed how she/he acted with prudence to achieve her/his goal and considered carefully to succeed.

Later he passed to meditation.

How miserable and annihilated I feel at the thought of how the wisdom of God comes down to speak to a base creature as I am! //

14 April 1889. 18th Speech: meekness and humility. I explained or rather my Good explained what should be true humility; in the same way how meekness is necessary for a Daughter of St. Anne. I continued for a good hour and before I did not know how to say anything. It was painful to be lacking one thought connected to another to make a speech.

In addition to hearing being said: “Go ahead, go ahead”, deep down there is no understanding of what is said. //

5 May 1889. 19 Conference: on modesty and purity, on detachment from parents, on the exact observance of the Constitutions.

Since these chapters are small, I gathered them together and explained them at the same time.

Silence on the streets was recommended very much and also to keep themselves away from looking through the windows and into the shops.

My Love, now I have no doubt of not succeeding; how well you speak! I assure you that I feel much pleasure as I speak and after I remember nothing. I say pleasure because

I have no difficulty and I like very much what you say… //

12 May. 20th Conference: right intention.

I stressed human respect very much and still more in teaching them to take possession of the most holy heart of the Virgin Mary, and how we can be open to feel her sweet love. How to run away from praises doing everything with the right objective, not to be overcome by selfishness and by human respect which is an intimate friend of pride. The one who cultivates human respect will certainly little by little become proud. //

26 May. 21st Conference: article 5, on the manner of relating with different people.

With the superiors: I was discouraged for the fear of not being able to explain this point, having completely nothing in mind. I was unable to gather anything. I was feeling completely like an empty bucket.

  • Well, my Jesus - I said – if it is your will that I do the conference, you will tell me and you will give words to this ass and it will repeat what you will suggest.

That was what happened; I explained with zeal this article. //

2 June. 22nd Conference

With the sisters and with the outsiders in the parlor. //

30 May. I had a brief Conference or rather an exhortation to the newly clothed encouraging them to sacrifice themselves to achieve holiness. I said that we must be stripped of the old man and be clothed with the nuptial habits. After I would have liked to say much on what I saw in the heart of certain people who were cool with God and gave themselves without the interior fervor and not knowing what an important thing they were doing. I kept quiet and I tried to take as a theme another argument fearing that something could escape me, but my God, my wisest Master, spoke enough to encourage those creatures. //

2 June 1889. Dedication of the month to the dress of Mary, as a way of handing oneself fully to the Blessed Virgin. I do not remember what I said as usual. I spoke but I remembered nothing, not knowing what I said since it was not my stuff.

I questioned the novices about meditation and I found them very capable. Oh, how I was pleased at the thought that my God every morning has fifty-five creatures meditating on his passion for three quarters of an hour!

2. THEMES OF HUMAN AND RELIGIOUS FORMATION

FROM 13 APRIL TO 8 DECEMBER 1890

MS 10. 2 – pp. 1 – 34

MS 10. 4 – pp. 1 – 13

MS 10. 2 – pp. 34 -44

Date 13 April 1890. Explanations of the Rule and meditation. 1st Conference.

To try to put into focus the scope for which we are dedicated to the Institute and have the Rule is before all else to sanctify ourselves so that we can sanctify the others with the exercise of charity. In actions we must continually practice charity and this should distinguish us in all. It cannot be denied that everything done out of charity is easy and one feels satisfaction in having done something for the Lord. //

Sunday, 20 April 1890. Explanation of the Rule and meditation. 2nd Conference

Gossiping fails in charity. It was shown how a failure in charity towards the sisters can be manifested in different ways. I spoke without knowing what I had to say and I was not ready with the theme. I am truly the slave of my God in all my actions! If I should write what I said I would not be able because I do not remember it. //

Sunday, 27 April 1890. 3rd Speech: meditation and explanation of the Rule.

As I promised I spoke on charity continuing the theme of last Sunday. I said that there is more sublime charity, more delicate and greater, very dear to our Crucifix; I asked them to tell me about this charity.

  • It is this one – I said – it is that one which a person has when she is stripped of everything she needs and makes of

it a gift. She always finds means to sacrifice herself and relieve the others and her sisters depriving herself of what pleases her // and would be necessary for her. She considers that one desires it and would be pleased even if she must deprive herself of what she needs for example… And I brought comparisons of what the saints did: Saint Francis of Assisi, Saint Francis of Sales etc. They never had a thought for themselves but they were intent on satisfying their charity in which they were eager. Let us look to ourselves, do we have this spirit? Alas, when we miss something small // and the directress takes it away how we take offence! To be deprived willingly? Not at all! And if we see that what was signed for us is given to another one only because it has the number belonging to us, what fear that it might be used up or because that one might own it definitively! Is this the charity of Jesus? Can such a Daughter of St. Anne be said to have charity and be really a bride // of the Crucified? Aren’t you bold! If you think you are such, answer me? Show me the uniform that you wear to be a follower of the Crucified! Where is the charity which makes you similar to him, where is the detachment from the earthly things? The relatives always in your head, many foolish attachments to frivolous things – detach yourself well from anything and then you will tell me that you are a follower of the Crucified.

We passed to the meditation questioning all, or at least a portion. //

4 May 1890. 4th Conference: explanation of the Rule on poverty.

As I questioned, they themselves explained the chapter.

The same was with the stuff which contains their number;

how they intend to have it. After meditation a good message was considered. They were taught how they should greet the sisters, a religious greeting not an artificial one. The same on the streets.

Among all there should be lovableness and sweetness;

never putting hands upon another! // The same should be in the garden; they must not stay one over the other, that is, very close one to the other.

How they should greet a person who comes to the novitiate; if a Monsignor or a Bishop comes, they should ask for his blessing, if a simple priest or a gentleman he is greeted. The same should be for a lady. Religious manners are delicate, they have nothing artificial and at the same time one behaves kindly and decently. One sacrifices her opinion to please the others. How beautiful our dwelling place is where without realizing we take big steps towards the heavenly throne. //

11 May 1890. 5th Conference: explanation of the Rule. I called one by one the professed sisters to teach religious manners.

When you enter a house where there are people… After finishing asking questions on meditation I continued on the manner of staying at table where a sister does a favor, helps (she could do it for a quarter of an hour since it is something urgent), the sister should thank her. I spoke on the need of staying straight, not to walk moving on the sides; a practical lesson was given. Passing before a sister even if a young one, use always // the word “may I”. Ask how they do when they get up, where their mind is, when they dress, how and which care they take to be modest in everything. Ask the sisters always: “Please for charity’s sake, do this or that for me.” //

Sunday, 18 May 1890. 6th Conference: explanation of the Rule by the same sisters.

How they should behave when they are in the houses in order to write to the superiors, to the general when she will be there because certainly I will not live forever. In this way they will learn about their duty, submission and respect. When writing to the superiors, think that they occupy the place of the Lord. In the same way be careful when speaking about them; never criticize their actions.

I would like to know if a sister who arrives greets with: “Blessed be our glorious Mother St. Anne…” Do you say it? //

25 May 1890. 7th Conference: the love of God.

Explanation of the Rule, and recitation of the same to a point of creating a moment of discussion.

As soon as they enter the house where they are destined, after our greeting, the glory is said and then to work. The stuff they are given to carry is handed over to the superior or to another. If the journey has been long and tiresome having spent the night, one should humbly ask the superior or the one on her behalf the permission to rest. Then // a good sister goes to work; she does not wait for orders to move, no. It is true that she is new and does not know how and where to start, but our activities are all the same. The house is different but the customs are always the same. It is very beautiful to see the sister at work as soon as she arrives as if she had been a thousand years in that house and she always finds something to do.

I assure you that immediately they get a good impression and the sisters // of that house get a good impression and the superior is consoled with the good person she received.

Instead when they arrive and start asking, if unfortunately they meet a sister who is used to gossip, soon they will be united and they start listening and gossiping. As soon as she finishes what she has been ordered, she searches for the sister to continue the chatter. I received a good impression from certain superiors who // as soon as they reached to their destination, they started their work; they worked with their hands and went ahead here and there. They always find work just as if they should never leave. Oh, these ones, yes, they are true Daughters of St. Anne!

They work only for one Institute, one house, and they are only one heart, all united; the houses are for them like one. What a beautiful consolation the Holy Mother will have, and how much blessing will they receive from heaven!

These are the unshakable columns of the Institute who… //

Monday 26 May: St. Philip. 8th Conference: Rule and some warnings.

A novice should be admonished and must kiss the feet of all. She will be told the way in which they should behave with the workers and how a religious should avoid them. They will ask me: “If he is a young man!” The same. This, however, since he is always in the house the behavior should be more severe (…).

It is recommended to the directress to let them put on the big veil for the journey and then the meditation… //

Find out what catechism the directress uses and ask her to explain a chapter. It will always be done like this because many times they must teach it and the same is for ourselves who need it. For the doctrine I will try to come on Thursday. //

Thursday 29 may 1890. 9th Conference

I taught them something on good manners. How they should close the doors and also when it is windy one should not say: “Closing is not my duty, therefore it is better I leave…”

Another point: how one should behave outside if it is night, if it is licit to speak and the eyes…

The responsibility of the works and the one for embroidery will be chosen and a small conference on charity will be given; after I will pass to the Christian doctrine in a practical way. //

1st June 1890. 10th Conference

The dedication of the month of May to the Blessed Virgin was done with a special conference, but brief. The Rule and then the meditation followed. I taught the sisters how to carry the Crucifix, what they should do and never to despise it. How they should stay in the church and in the moment of the homily and other small things. //

5 June 1890. 11th Conference: explanation of the catechism.

Do it in a way that they memorize it and a sister should explain it.

A word was said on the month dedicated to the Sacred

Heart.

Recommend to be especially modest this month to please Jesus. //

12th Conference: recitation of the Rule and of the catechism, meditation and report of the month of the Sacred Heart.

Inculcate the devotion of spiritual communions which can be done well only through silence. All the actions done in the presence of God are done well and according to his will. In everything we must do, let us question the Lord before the action. // How do we feel in our hearts? Whom should we listen to as we question the Lord in order to pass a judgment if it is good or not. //

15 June 1890. 13 Conference: explanation of the Rule.

Speak of what reverence we should have for the Rule and what kind of love in observing it because in this we have all our good. //

22 June 1890. 14 Conference: recitation of the rule, in addition some explanation of the same. Meditation and conference on humility and on the love for the Institute.

How a superior should relate with the subjects to be loved. Question a subject in the manner of relating with a superior. In fact they asked for instructions. I represented the subject and they the superiors. //

24 June 1890. 15th Conference: recitation of the Rule and explanation. Additional recitation of the catechism, explanation, meditation and then questions on the various points of the Rule and on the duties of the superior.

Formulate a dialogue in which the sister represents the superior and I the subject.

… having a spiteful, touchy, behavior with tendencies to plot and gossip, put together calumnies and suspicions that the superior steals or makes savings // at the expense of the hospital, hides the linen and has no scruple to give it if it strikes her fancy. What a Rule!

She does not wish to receive Communion, and her conscience pricks her; finally she becomes quick-tempered and the sisters inform the superior, but she answers:

  • If money is needed, what should I do?

And the sisters:

  • Let us write to the Mother who will certainly provide a remedy; but if the superior is aware that we write, woe betide! // Immediately she will suspect that we are writing against her and she will pout. Poor us, we have ended living; certainly she will make us pay for it!

R. The superior cannot reach this point, these are your suspicions; furthermore a superior who knows how to manage and who really keeps that place for obedience, desires nothing other than that the sisters write in that way. If she will be told what to do, she will always be happy.

D. Sister: I take courage // I write; let her like or dislike me; in the name of the Lord I will send the letter. May everything be for God’s greater glory. //

25 June. 16th Conference: day of recollection

The person who loves Jesus cannot get angry with the creatures but speaks meekly while they accuse her…

R. I cannot avoid feeling offended. Oh, what do you say? If you are a superior, where there is a case of correction you must do it with zeal and strength, never with anger and grudge. Tell me: one cannot have this virtue unless one has a low concept of oneself, awareness of being nothing. //

Tell me something, someone tells me:

  • What can we do in order to have these virtues if we do not have someone to guide us, a good director, and a chosen preacher who can give us spiritual conferences?

I tell you that when a person wants to give herself completely to God and love him truly she strips herself of everything that is earthly and seeks God fully and in everything. //

1st July 1890. 17th Conference: the circular and the order in novitiate. The usual explanation of the Rule, meditation and catechism.

How should one who has been a superior and then discharged behave? She should behave as the saints who always desired the least places.

What about the complaint because of being discharged and saying: “Why was I discharged?” No, she should better say: “I am pleased.”

Why think of being slandered? //

There one suspects that they are the sisters, the confessor…

  • Oh - one says – I am really under a hard trial! I do not feel like staying here, in punishment in the Mother House without any duty! //

6 July 1890. 18th Conference

A summary was done of everything that was said in the past. It was done in a way that they may learn the Rule by heart and also the catechism and the religious manners,

French language and the other studies: piano etc.

A word was said on how there should be peace and love among the sisters; there is no love that derives from a bond of flesh and blood that can equal charity, no. Many examples of saints and what they did were mentioned.

MS 10. 4 – pp. 1 – 13

Piacenza, 13 July. 1st Conference1

Reading and explaining the Rule. Meditation: questioning and repetition. Religious manners: teaching it practically. A word of …//

Piacenza, 20 July. 2nd Conference. Explanation of the Rule; explanation of the doctrine, meditation.

Here I should stop to tell them that they are not punctual for the meditation, that they sleep and as soon as the directress will find one that sleeps she will send her out of the church. In this way she will be obliged to meditate outside, kneeling. The same is for the prayers: they say them badly and unruly and one cannot imagine the grumbling… //

27 July. 3rd Conference: Humility

Without humility there is no entry to heaven.

There are three crosses and three are the ways of carrying the cross. There are those who carry it on their shoulders and they carry it for the love of God, but they feel the burden very much. They do not put it down, but they implore a bit to be fortified and have strength to continue their journey never putting it down. These are the souls for whom heaven is assured. //

Next there are those souls who desire perfection and love much; these carry the cross tightly on their breast and never remove it. They bear the weight of the same which some times crushes their bones, but in the suffering they find joy and they keep it always more tightly. These souls are favored with strength by the Lord and certainly they reach the port of the blessed eternity they desire.

The third way of carrying the cross is that of the real lovers of the Lord, who know no other comfort than suffering. // These carry it tightly in their hearts and suck the worm-wood of the cross which the dear and beloved

Saviour drank. The essence of suffering is this: suffering with resignation, without seeking the least comfort, only suffering.

Their relief is weeping in secret at the feet of the Lord;

squeezing against their breast the holy cross, love of the seraphim and the joy of those who love.

These are the souls who enjoy the places of seraphim. //

Thursday 31 August. 4th Conference: the subtlety of selfishness and of its two companions: gratification of honor and vain glory. The three of them are grafted on us, as they try to put out their heads and they are like the smoke. If we keep vigilant not allowing them to come out, little by little they vanish. The thickest smoke is that of selfishness, which is not easy to subdue; the same is for vain glory, gratification remains and this is very difficult to // vanish because it is so closely identified with our nature that it requires careful study to realize it. Many times this is as boring as the big flies; I say it for those souls who aim at perfection.

It is felt in all the actions because a “clever!” received makes us come up and show off bringing in our hearts something that… Meanwhile what happens?

However, this one for now I will leave. I limit myself to telling you to run away from it. //

For having given in to the gratification of honor immediately one should try to find the way…

  • My Jesus – one should say – I am not the one but you who have done this!

Then one gives a look… Today this and tomorrow?

Within a day the good that has been done is forgotten and with this all the actions. The same creature rebels and there is today hosanna and tomorrow “crucify,” sufferings etc.

Teach to meditate and to study the Rule. //

Piacenza, August (…) 5th Conference: how they should meditate; after we will pass to the catechism and to the recitation of the Rule. All the points of the Rule will be touched on and explained. It will be concluded with a few words on obedience. //

12 September (…) 6th Conference

The wounds of religious communities are three and these carry a horrible stinking gangrene with them that wear away the soul; it infects it with germs and the body takes the shape of a serpent it always tries to penetrate on all sides and with strength spits out its poison provided one is satisfied in defaming the neighbor.

Do you see her anxious? Woe betide if she is reproached! She is the creature, // the most innocent that could be and with the others of her kind throw out phrases of horrible grumbling.

I came across one case! After having called one to her duty exhorting her to cease grumbling, not at all! She started to excuse herself to sail… I kept quiet to see where it would end. Oh, who could believe it? She ended up blaming herself such that she seemed to be speaking in the third person. Really odd! Then I could not do other than laugh: this was as the slave in the galley // or as the imprisonment that stole herself to satisfy this vice. //

28 September: Conference on selfishness, a second gangrene. Explanation of the Rule and meditation.

MS 10. 2 – pp. 34 – 44

2 November 1890. Rome. 19th Conference. Explanation of the Rule, catechism, meditation and a brief speech. I suffered much because I was able to say very little with difficulty… //

3rd November 1890. Explanation of the Rule, catechism and meditation.

20th Conference.

The two monsters of these days, disproportionately big that struggled one against the other. One had the mission to save the souls in the world and the other one the religious.

//

Rome, 6 November 1890. 21st Conference. Catechism, explanation of the Rule, meditation.

Can I be in the presence of God while I treat temporal things?

How do I find myself? The mind thinks and the intellect is always in his presence.

How can one understand that in all her actions she seeks nothing other than the glory of God? Anything, even the smallest that is against his will, is imperfect and it is not committed with fear of offending God since one is in his presence. // How can this be acquired? Repeating often:

“God sees me.”

Out of fear of offending him turn your eyes to him and give up committing many imperfections. Lovers of suffering and desirous of the burden of the cross, bed of the faithful brides, lovers of Jesus his truly beloved, they only feel sweetness and love, always resting on his sweet bed warm with love. Only the cross gathered all the essence of suffering // that was consumed on it.

I tried to show them the beauty and the greatness of the holy cross pausing every now and then to ask for an explanation of what was said. //

30 November 1890. 22nd Conference. First the catechism then the explanation of the Rule and the meditation.

A humble person is gentle in her manners; she is unable to offend others. A humble person never considers herself to be someone; she owns much because humility is a hidden fruitful treasure and its fruit is the love of God. Only to the humble is this given. // A humble person does not know selfishness, is respectful and does not offend. Many times she is called ignorant, but this is an excuse. I will bring an example of a holy farmer who did not know how to read or write and yet she was very polite… //

4 December, 1890. 23rd Conference. Explanation of the Rule, catechism and meditation.

What a superior should do for the economy of the house and in this way show the management against the wrong way of doing of certain sisters. If they are teachers they say: “We have earned them and we want to eat well” and “The superior wants to save money to give it to the Mother” etc. In the same way: “We want books, stuff…” they are never happy.

Finally on the vow of poverty // we do not want to hear anything. It is very bad to see a sister wasting everything. She does not want to know of anything and she is always careful to see if the stuff is sent to the Mother House. In the same way they have no scruple to keep money in their pockets. //

8 December: feast of the Immaculate Virgin Mary

All beautiful is Mary, radiant is her face, while as a lily and shining with glory in the midst of angels. The pleasure of the Father, the delight of the Son, the love of the Holy

Spirit: Mary!

Among the Seraphim a white dove, most pure Virgin!

The radiance of the Virgin dazzled those spirits inflamed with love and they resounded with new joy. Mary all pure!

The Cherubim raised a song, the Thrones, the Powers joined with angelic voices singing: “Tota pulchra, you are beautiful Mary!”

The Archangels saluted her with reverence // with the title: “Immaculate, Sovereign of heaven and earth”

respectful in a profound act of homage to Mary.

Another sound of the blessed spirits embarked their song: “There is no original stain in you.”

Queen of angels, heaven and earth bow before you and only one cry is heard: “Mary, you are Immaculate.”

The good souls resounded their prayers: in heaven, pray for us poor sinners, Mary shining seal…

3. THEMES OF HUMAN AND RELIGIOUS FORMATION

FROM 15 NOVEMBER 1891 TO 8 JANUARY 1893

MS 10. 3 – pp. 1 – 22

My daughters, in which way do we follow him? In the will? For this one I can assure you we perfectly follow our own. My God! Perhaps in the love? Is it not the love of God that drove you to become religious and be away from //

Ignatius through a strong impulse, St. Paul // on having fallen from a horse, St. Margaret in entering a church…

Tell me, how do you answer this love; do you love? How do you love the Institute, the Work of God? How do you work? With what kind of spirit? We have forgotten obedience; it seems that for the superior it should not exist.

They know very well how to impose it on their subjects and they want it to be done blindly; woe betides if they do not do it!

In what does obedience consist of for us? I seem to hear a voice which tells me: “In love you will discover what this virtue demands of you.” //

Will and Love. 2nd Conference

What does obedience demand of a superior? Here is a superior who has this office for the love she has for the Work of God. She obeys everything that the major superiors order her: bearing with patience the behaviors of the sisters, taking upon herself their pain and labor, relieving them with acts of equal benevolence without grimace but with true charity and love of a mother. //

It is heard being said: - Doing this bothers me.

And the superior: - Oh, she is a wayward sister, who came out of the novitiate with no spirit. What kind of people they admit! She has no vocation; they should do better selection!

Horror! Put yourself at the feet of the Crucifix and look at yourself: who is more helpless, the poor young or you? What would happen if they could have done this with you? Meanwhile the other sisters listen to this horrible grumbling against the major superiors and the Institute; it is a scandal. Tell me, when Jesus was a child and obeyed St. Joseph and Mary // doing the services with those sweet and delicate small hands, he could well say to the Eternal Father he did not like to live with St. Joseph and ask him to send an array of angels who could have served him and understood him better! But because of obedience, he had to do this for the love of thankless humankind. //

Obedience and Love. 3rd Conference

A superior who ill-treats the sisters even before the outsiders, leaves them alone in the duties, in the hospital, in kindergarten, now with one and now with the other, can she say that she loves and guides them? The president, the confessor etc. comes and she does everything and is everything. She treats // the poor sisters as stupid, capable of nothing. I ask you, how does this superior behave?

  • Oh – it is said – I will write to the Mother very clearly what subjects she sends.

Meanwhile the poor novices remain scandalized and they start to say: “It is better to remove my habit and go back home instead of staying here.”
